t: EMPLOYEE HEALTH EDUCATION AND EXPOSURE PROTOCOL

l: The Fort Worth Police Department is concerned with the health and well-being of its employees. In an effort to facilitate compliance with state and federal laws concerning communicable disease protection and best practices for emerging health and safety issues, the police department has developed this employee health care and exposure protocol which is administered through Policy Management and Safety.

Each class of recruits, full-time and reserve, will receive four (4) hours of training and education in the area of communicable disease which will include all required elements as set forth by the Texas Department of Health. Instruction will include modes of transmission for all at-risk communicable diseases, methods of prevention of transmission, behaviors that create a potential risk for infection, and procedures for line of duty exposure incidents. Vaccinations, when available, for diseases that present a high risk for occupational exposure will be offered during the four (4) hour training.

Training or Roll Call bulletins will be developed to inform employees of new health and safety developments or procedures, as needed. Commanders/Captains will ensure that periodic roll-call and workplace training is conducted. Commanders/Captains will also ensure that up-to-date equipment and supplies are readily available, providing instructions for their proper use.

The police department will recognize and utilize Universal Precautions which state that when emergency medical and public safety workers encounter body fluids under uncontrolled, emergency circumstances in which differentiation between fluid types is difficult, if not impossible, they should treat all body fluids as potentially hazardous. In circumstances where it is difficult or impossible to differentiate between fluid types, employees shall assume that the fluid is potentially infectious and use the appropriate level of personal protective equipment (PPE).
B. Infectious Disease Control Supplies and Engineering Controls

1. All divisions are responsible for ordering and maintaining an adequate supply of commonly needed infectious disease control supplies unique to their duties. Supervisors shall maintain the control and the proper storage in a convenient location of adequate infectious disease control and personal protective equipment (PPE) supplies for their units. Protective gloves, disinfecting materials, and first-aid supplies shall be made readily available at all times. Hypoallergenic alternatives must be available to employees who have an allergic sensitivity to protective equipment. It will be the responsibility of the employee to maintain their supply of any item(s). Infectious disease control supplies will consist of, but not be limited to, the following items:
a. Disposable gloves. Latex-free gloves should be made available to personnel who have an allergic sensitivity to latex
b. Antimicrobial towelettes, gels, or sprays
c. Liquid soap available at all sink areas
e. Additional items, depending on assignment, may include:
2. Officers shall keep disposable gloves in their possession while on patrol.

3. Puncture-resistant sharps containers shall be utilized for disposal and transport of sharps and the submission of evidence to the Crime Lab, Property Room, or other units as necessary. To prevent injuries, used needles shall not be recapped, broken, or bent.
4. All working surfaces and equipment that could have become contaminated shall be cleaned and checked routinely and shall be decontaminated as necessary.

a. Supervisors for work assignments that require continual staffing at the same workstation shall ensure that additional precautions to disinfect the work area are performed at the end of each shift. Specific disinfectants for the work area shall be readily available for use by the employees.

5. A “spit sock” or similar product which safely covers the mouth without interfering with breathing may be used on a suspect that is spitting on officers. The spit sock will be utilized in situations where a suspect presents a viable danger to the officer for exposure to infectious disease and with the officer following proper departmental tactical guidelines for the product.
6. Contaminated vehicles will be taken to the city service center, marked as biohazard, for proper decontamination.

7. Before submission to the Crime Lab and/or Property Room, any evidence that is suspected of being contaminated by body fluids shall be placed in a leak-proof container or package and marked as biohazard.

A. Any employee who has been bitten by a person, stuck by a needle, or who has had direct physical contact with a potentially infected person or bodily fluids of an infected person, while in the line of duty, shall be considered to have been exposed. Employees who contract a contagious disease that may be transmitted from one person to another via work-related contact are expected to seek appropriate medical attention and remain off work until medically approved to return to the workplace.

B. Any employee coming to work suspected of having a contagious or communicable disease that could significantly impact others in the workplace, may be required by the applicable commander/captain/manager to leave the workplace and remain off work until such time that the infected employee may no longer transmit the disease to another person via work-related contact.
1. By City of Fort Worth regulations, the employee would be required to use accrued leave or be on leave without pay if no accrued leave is available.
2. The supervisor may require the employee to provide to the Police Department Medical Records Custodian (MRC) a medical release from a medical doctor before allowing the employee to return to work.

C. The police department will make available, free of charge and at a reasonable time and place, the Hepatitis A and B vaccines, influenza vaccine, and tetanus vaccine at the recommended vaccination series schedule to all employees who are at risk of occupational exposure. Any additional vaccinations, booster doses, or titers recommended by the U.S. Public Health Service to avoid risk of occupational exposure will also be provided upon request.
The employee experiencing a possible exposure to an infectious disease shall:
1. Immediately cleanse and disinfect the exposed area, if possible.
3. For sworn personnel, assist in delivering suspect/source to hospital, if possible. It is recommended the source and exposed officer are treated at the same hospital.
4. If appropriate, preserve and collect any physical evidence pertaining to the exposure.

5. Even if medical attention was delivered by a hospital, the employee shall visit the city-designated medical health care facility within ten (10) days for a medical needs assessment/follow-up and for the result of the source’s blood test.

a. To qualify for Workers’ Compensation or any similar benefits, it must be documented that within ten (10) days of the exposure, the employee had a test result that indicated an absence of the reportable disease, including HIV.

b. If the employee is electing to refuse testing, the employee must sign the Testing Upon Possible Exposure to Reportable Disease Waiver (FWPD-91, Rev 11/02) form. Employees shall be made aware that refusal to be tested may result in loss of workers compensation and similar benefits.

6. For sworn personnel, complete a Support of Mandatory Testing Affidavit for all exposures with the date and circumstances of the incident to be forwarded to the police department Health and Exposure Coordinator and the Injury Report email link.
1. Immediately have Communications contact the Police Tactical Medic. The Police Tactical Medic will coordinate with the hospital staff and will complete all employee exposure paperwork.
a. If for any reason a Police Tactical Medic is not available and the supervisor has questions on how to handle an exposure, the supervisor should contact the Health and Exposure Coordinator.

2. If emergency treatment of the employee is necessary, have the employee taken to an area hospital. Whenever feasible, it is preferable the employee and source are taken to the same hospital, but it is not required in the case of an emergency.
a. If an employee is admitted to the hospital for a length of time, complete DWC-1 and IOC with as much available information at the time.
b. If requested, have the health care provider (hospital) contact the Police Medical Records Custodian(s) concerning authorization for assessment, testing, treatment and/or prescriptions.
c. When the employee is discharged from the hospital, advise the employee to contact the city-designated medical health care facility for follow-up of the exposure.

3. For sworn personnel, if the officer will not require emergency treatment, the supervisor shall immediately ensure the officer and the source are taken to the same hospital and that voluntary consent from the suspect/source to test for infectious disease is requested by hospital staff.
a. The officer experiencing the exposure should not request, nor be in the presence of the source, when the source is asked for voluntary consent.
b. When the hospital staff requests the consent, their staff will complete their required consent forms and the police department consent form will not be necessary.

c. If the Tactical Medic has not arrived at the hospital and the supervisor is placed in a position to request consent of the source, the supervisor shall have the suspect/source sign a Consent/Refusal to Draw Blood (FWPD-75, Rev. 11/03) form denoting decision.
(1) The Supervisor shall request the MRN (medical record number) for the source from the hospital staff. This number is necessary to obtain the test results of the source.

d. If the suspect/source refuses to be tested and the Tactical Medic has not arrived at the hospital, the supervisor should have Communications contact the Tactical Medic or the department Health and Exposure Coordinator immediately.

e. When the employee is prescribed medications and must fill the prescription at night or on a weekend, if the pharmacy requests a claim number for insurance or other information for payment, contact either the Tactical Medic or the Department Health and Exposure Coordinator for assistance.

4. If the suspect/source is deceased, contact the Tactical Medic immediately. The Tactical Medic will coordinate with the Medical Examiner’s office for the blood draw and delivering the blood sample from the Medical Examiner to the designated laboratory.

5. In addition to exposures, supervisors should be cognizant at all times of unusual medical situations involving their personnel. If a situation appears to be possibly communicable or a threat to the employee or to public health, the supervisor will immediately contact the Police Department’s Health and Exposure Coordinator.

6. For sworn personnel, if an Administrative Order must be served on a source who has refused consent, a supervisor will assist the Tactical Medic, Major Case, or the Health and Exposure Coordinator in locating the source and serving the Administrative Order. If the exposed employee is a Fort Worth Fire Department firefighter or paramedic, a police supervisor in the district where the source will be served will assist the Fort Worth Fire Department in serving the Administrative Order if requested.

1. When contacted by the employee’s supervisor or Communications personnel, the Tactical Medic will respond to all exposures, either by phone or in-person. When contacted by a person other than the supervisor or Communications personnel and the situation may warrant a department response, verify that the department's Health and Exposure Coordinator is aware of the situation.
2. Ensure all required forms are completed and filed with appropriate personnel. Required forms include:
a. The First Report of Injury form (DWC-1) and IOC

b. The Infectious Exposure Cases Checklist (FWPD-56, Rev.12/18) and e-mail the checklist to the department’s Health and Exposure Coordinator. The source’s hospital MRN will be placed on the Checklist. If the employee is tested at the hospital, the employee’s MRN will also be placed on the Checklist.
c. For sworn personnel, the Support of Mandatory Testing Affidavit.

NOTE: If the employee refuses medical attention or testing, the Testing Upon Possible Exposure to Reportable Disease Waiver is necessary. Ensure that the employee is aware that refusal to be tested may result in loss of workers compensation and similar benefits.
a. Contact the hospital staff if the source cannot be immediately tested and request the testing be done as soon as possible.
b. Contact the medical examiner if the source is deceased and follow the chain of custody for source testing.
c. Assist in locating the source, when necessary.
d. When the source has refused voluntary testing, work with the Department’s Health and Exposure Coordinator to notify the County Health Department for an Administrative Affidavit.

e. If the source refuses the County Health Department Administrative Affidavit for testing, work with the Department’s Health and Exposure Coordinator and/or Major Case to contact the District Attorney’s Office for a court order.

4. If the department Health and Exposure Coordinator is unavailable for an extended period, assist employees and/or supervisors with concerns and provide notifications to the hospital infectious disease staff for test results.
D. Department Health and Exposure Coordinator’s Responsibility
1. Oversee the Communicable Disease Program for the Police Department and coordinate with Tactical Medics on all elements on employee exposures.
2. For sworn personnel, ensure the Exposure Risk Office in the hospital is notified of the exposure for return of the test results in a timely manner.
3. Act as a liaison between the police department and other agencies on infectious disease exposures or required vaccinations, if applicable.
4. Immediately notify Major Case of any situation with possible criminal implications.
a. In the case of a possible criminal case, Major Case shall determine the appropriate investigative entity.
5. Notify the Public Information Officer of any situation that may involve the media or overall department.
6. Handle all exposure incidents with strict confidentiality, observing all federal and state privacy laws. Maintaining strict confidentiality, track the statistical data on all exposures.
7. Assist with all unusual or difficult exposure or health situations.
8. Coordinate with appropriate entities on necessary court orders and administrative orders.
9. Disclose exposure information only as authorized by law and only to authorized parties to uphold privacy.
10. Develop and maintain the police department’s Model Exposure Control Plan which shall meet all mandatory federal and state regulations.

1. All personnel are restricted in what can be conveyed to employees, other emergency personnel, or citizens concerning medical information, most notably HIV/AIDS. Information regarding persons suspected of being infected with HIV/AIDS must be kept strictly confidential and cannot be transmitted across the radio or the MDCs. Disclosure of test results or other confidential HIV/AIDS-related information carries both civil and criminal penalties.
a. Do not place any sensitive information related to the exposure in the offense/incident report summary.

2. Based on the Federal Privacy Act, the Texas Commission on Human Rights Act, and the Texas Communicable Disease Prevention and Control Act, any medical documentation or information provided by an HIV/AIDS-infected employee to medical or management personnel must be considered confidential and private information. As such, employers are forbidden by law to disclose this information without the employee’s knowledge and consent, except as required by Public Health laws.
3. All personnel should be knowledgeable on the Health Insurance Portability Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA) and only disclose information when authorized under the law enforcement exceptions.

A. When engineering controls and/or administrative actions do not provide sufficient protection for personnel, use of Hearing Protection Devices (HPD) or, if conditions mandate, a combination of hearing protection devices to ensure personnel’s hearing is being protected.
B. The Fort Worth Police Department has areas and locations where hearing protection is required by all persons in that area.
1. Compliance and adherence to this requirement is not optional.
2. Employees who refuse to wear the hearing protection device (HPD) as required will not be allowed access/entrance to those areas.

3. Employees found to be non-compliant in wearing required HPDs will be removed from the area and notification will be made to their supervisor. The employee will be restricted from the area(s) until proper HPDs is worn as required.
C. When an employee experiences an unusual noise exposure, including firing a weapon without hearing protection, the employee is to report event to their supervisor in a timely manner.
1. The supervisor shall immediately initiate the process for testing and evaluation and will complete an Injury/Illness form (DWC-1).
2. In the event an employee is exposed to sound energy, such that they feel their hearing has been affected by the exposure, they have the right to file an injury claim.

D. Any employee firing any weapon without hearing protection shall have their supervisor complete an injury/illness form (DWC-1) immediately. This will include officers and any police personnel in close proximity to the firing. This does include officers firing their weapon in the field during an officer-involved shooting.

E. Due to the unusual noise exposure, personnel in units such as the Weapon Range, SWAT, and Crime Lab (firearms) shall be tested annually for potential hearing loss as well as lead and zinc levels in their blood. Screening will be completed by August 31 of each year and be performed by the City of Fort Worth designated health provider indicated for this series of testing.

items.t: CARDIAC HEALTH AND AUTOMATED EXTERNAL DEFIBRILLATOR (AED)
l: A. An automated external defibrillator (AED) is a medical device designed to analyze the heart rhythm and deliver an electric shock to victims of ventricular fibrillation to restore the heart rhythm to normal.

B. An AED is located in each staffed police facility throughout the department. All personnel within the facility will be trained on the use of the AED and be aware of the location(s) of the AED unit. Employees shall notify their supervisor if any problems with the AED are noted such as:
1. A low battery signal or other maintenance issues
2. An employee uses the AED or is aware of its recent use
3. Any additional items such as pads or a Stop the Bleed kit are missing from the cabinet or have expired.
Supervisors will be responsible for contacting the AED Coordinator when notified by an employee of incident.
